shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, which reduces variety and moves me away from a balanced bundle. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility.

Currently I have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another A would give me 2 A, 0 B, 1 C — creating an imbalance and leaving me with zero of a good, which reduces variety and lowers my utility. I prefer to keep balanced holdings.

Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - losing all variety in B while stacking up on A, which I value less due to diminishing returns from having more of it. This decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 1A, 0B, 2C, reducing variety since I'd go from equal 1-1-1 to an uneven bundle. Since I value variety, this trade decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

Trading away my only B (going to 0) to get a second C would leave me with 1A/0B/3C, which is more imbalanced and reduces variety value. I'd rather keep a diverse bundle of 1/1/1 or trade for something that increases variety instead.

I currently have equal quantities of A, B, and C (1 each). Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and making my bundle less balanced. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility, so I decline.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another A would make me 2 A/0 B/1 C, creating imbalance and reducing variety value, which is worse under my preference for variety.

Currently I have equal 1-1-1 inventory, which I value for variety. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C — losing variety entirely and creating a lopsided bundle. This decreases my utility despite the numerical gain in total goods.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given I value diversity.

Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety (A:1, B:0, C:2). Since I value variety, this decreases my utility rather than increasing it. I'll decline this specific swap.

Trading away my only B would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a lopsided bundle (A1,B0,C3) instead of the balanced (A1,B1,C1) I have now. Since I value variety, losing my only unit of B for more C hurts my utility. I'd prefer a trade that keeps or increases variety, like trading A or C for something I have less of, or a smaller C-for-B swap that doesn't zero out B.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and creating an imbalance rather than improving my utility. I prefer to maintain or increase diversity across goods, so this trade doesn't benefit me.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away B for A would just shift which good I have 2 of and 0 of, not improving variety - it would make me have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C, which is less balanced than my current even distribution. This trade doesn't increase my utility.

Current bundle is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 more A would make me 3 A, 0 B, 1 C, which is highly unbalanced and reduces variety value even though total quantity increases. Better to seek a trade that maintains or improves diversity.

Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away C for B would just shift the imbalance to C=0, B=2, without improving variety - it's a lateral move that doesn't increase utility since I'd go from balanced to unbalanced.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 2 C and 0 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:2. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to A:1, B:1, C:2, which is more balanced across goods and increases variety-weighted utility since B was my scarcest good.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 2 C - trading away my entire stock of A is too costly. This would create a new scarcity in A while only mildly improving B. A fairer trade would be 1 A for 1 B, preserving balance across all three goods.
I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my inventory to 2/1/1, increasing overall utility.

A better trade would be 1C for 1B to balance my holdings without eliminating a good entirely.

I currently have 3 A, 0 B, 1 C, so my inventory is very unbalanced. Trading away 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) improves variety and balance, increasing my overall utility.

Giving up C to get B just swaps which good I have zero of, without net gain in variety. I'd rather keep C and seek a trade that gives me B without losing C, e.g. trading A for B instead.

Better to negotiate a 1-for-1 trade to maintain variety across all three goods.

Currently I have 0 A, 1 B, 1 C. Trading away my only B for A would just shift my shortage from A to B, keeping me at 0 in one good - no improvement in variety/balance. I'd rather acquire A while keeping my B, so I'll seek a trade that doesn't cost me my only unit of a good.

Currently I have 0 A, 1 B, 1 C. Trading away my only B (dropping to 0) for 2 A gives me a bundle of 2 A, 0 B, 1 C. This increases variety in A which I lack entirely, and since I value all goods equally but prefer diversity, gaining 2 units of a good I have none of outweighs losing my single B. Net utility improves since going from (0,1,1) to (2,0,1) adds more value from acquiring A than lost from B given diminishing marginal value of extra units - actually let's check: losing B (1->0) removes one unit of a scarce good too. But gaining 2 A is worth more than losing 1 B since A count goes from 0 to 2 (two units of a completely missing good) versus losing B's single unit. This still nets positive since I end with a more balanced-ish spread and higher total marginal utility.
This trade would leave me with B:2, C:0, A:0 — reducing variety and giving up my only C for a good I already have equally. It doesn't improve my bundle diversity, so I decline.

This specific 2-for-1 trade is unfavorable since it reduces my total goods count and leaves me with zero C, losing diversity.
